page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Additionally, the instance bundles 1890 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.15 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 2051.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Text processing and small-model LLM text generation also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as the stress-ng multi-core test at 7988.69 and Geekbench multi-core score at 7780.0, fall into the average tier. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in the Passmark memory score of 1716.72 and medium-model LLM text generation at 8.29 tokens/sec, which rank in the bottom 25% despite the large memory capacity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E32-8ds_v6 offers high memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU processing. The inclusion of 1890 GB of local storage reduces the need for external storage attachments for temporary data. This hardware profile is well-suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers, data buffering, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
